guides.title: Configuring Ergosfare
guides.description: Registration entry points, the two ways to select from the frozen composition table, and the knobs on AddErgosfare.
guides.body:
Everything Ergosfare needs at runtime comes from one call:

```csharp
services.AddErgosfare(o => o
    .AddCommandModule(c => c.RegisterGenerated())
    .AddQueryModule(q => q.RegisterGenerated())
    .AddEventModule(e => e.RegisterGenerated()));
```

`AddErgosfare` takes an `Action<IModuleRegistry>`. Each `AddXModule` call opens a module
builder that **selects** from the compiled composition table for this container. Only add the
modules you use — an application that never publishes events has no reason to register the
event module.

## Registration is selection

The source generator compiles the whole closure's handlers and interceptors into a frozen
composition table before the application runs. Registration does not discover anything; it
records which of that table's participant rows *this* container runs. Selection is a union,
so registering the same type twice — or through two different calls — is harmless.

A row nobody selected is not part of any pipeline, and a container that selected nothing runs
nothing. That is the whole failure model: a message with no selected handler raises
`NoHandlerFoundException`.

### Generated (preferred)

```csharp
.AddCommandModule(c => c.RegisterGenerated())
```

The bulk path. The generator names every command construct it discovered — in your
compilation *and in referenced assemblies* — and emits dispatch roots so Native AOT has a
static anchor for every generic instantiation. See
[Compile-time discovery](/ergosfare.docs/core-concepts/compile-time-discovery).

`RegisterGenerated("reporting.*")` narrows the same call to the constructs whose
[discovery keys](/ergosfare.docs/core-concepts/discovery-keys) match a pattern.

### Explicit

```csharp
.AddCommandModule(c => c
    .Register<CreateProductHandler>()
    .Register(typeof(LogCommands)))
```

Useful when you want a construct selected under conditions the generator cannot see — a
feature flag read from configuration, for example. The type still has to exist in the
compiled table; `Register<T>()` chooses, it does not add.

{% aside type="caution" %}
There is no third way. `RegisterFromAssembly(...)`, `RegisterDescriptors(...)` and the
`IMessageRegistry` surface were removed in v2.3 — a dynamically loaded assembly cannot append
a message shape after compilation. See
[Migrating from v2.2 to v2.3](/ergosfare.docs/migration/v2.2-to-v2.3).
{% /aside %}

## Handler lifetimes

Handlers and interceptors resolve from the **calling DI scope** on every dispatch. Their
lifetime is whatever you registered them as:

| Registration | Behaviour per dispatch |
|---|---|
| Singleton | Container-cached; one instance for the process |
| Scoped | One instance per DI scope |
| Transient | A new instance for every dispatch |

Transient handlers allocating once per dispatch is not a leak — it is what a transient
registration declares. For dispatch-heavy loops inside a single scope that want instance
reuse, either register handlers as singletons or opt in globally:

```csharp
services.AddErgosfare(o => o
    .ForceMemoizedHandlers()
    .AddCommandModule(c => c.RegisterGenerated()));
```

## Per-dispatch settings

Each module's mediator takes an optional settings object. It carries a group filter and a
seed for the context's item bag:

```csharp
var settings = new CommandMediationSettings
{
    Items = { ["tenant"] = tenantId }
};
settings.Filters.Groups = ["audit"];

await commands.SendAsync(new CreateProduct("Laptop", 999m), settings);
```

- **`Filters.Groups`** restricts the pipeline to handlers and interceptors carrying a
  matching `[Group]`. An empty collection means "everything registered". See
  [Groups and weights](/ergosfare.docs/cross-cutting-concerns/groups-and-weights).
- **`Items`** seeds `context.Items` for this dispatch.

Group filters participate in the pipeline plan cache key, so the filtering itself is done once
per `(message type, group set)` rather than per dispatch. A filtered dispatch is still not free
relative to an unfiltered one: **generated plans are only consulted for a group-less dispatch**,
so filtering means taking the general executor path. Prefer
[`GroupSet`](/ergosfare.docs/cross-cutting-concerns/groups-and-weights#groupset--the-reusable-filter)
over a fresh settings object when you do filter.

## Result adapters

When a handler returns a value-carried failure — a foreign `Result<T>` type — an
`IResultAdapter<TResult>` surfaces that failure out of the pipeline without the handler
throwing. The binding is declarative, per message:

```csharp
[ResultAdapter(typeof(MyResultAdapter))]
public sealed record CreateProduct(string Name) : ICommand<MyResult<Guid>>;
```

The framework's own `Result` / `Result<T>` carriers need no annotation, and an unannotated
message with any other result type is not probed at all. `[IgnoreResultAdapter]` opts a
message out.

For a codebase-wide carrier, configure one fallback instead of annotating every message:

```csharp
services.AddErgosfare(o => o
    .UseDefaultResultAdapter(typeof(MyResultAdapter<>))
    .AddCommandModule(c => c.RegisterGenerated()));
```

The type may be closed over one result type or an open generic definition closed per served
result; it needs a public parameterless constructor, and a bad type fails inside
`AddErgosfare` rather than on some first dispatch.

{% aside type="caution" %}
This binding surface is `[Experimental]` under **`ERGOEXP001`** — `[ResultAdapter]`,
`[IgnoreResultAdapter]` and `UseDefaultResultAdapter` alike. The value channel's semantics
are settled; the way you bind to it may still shift in a minor release. See
[Experimental APIs](/ergosfare.docs/advanced/experimental-apis).
{% /aside %}

## What is *not* configurable

Two omissions are deliberate:

- **The execution context exposes no service provider.** Handler resolution belongs to the
  dispatcher. If a handler needs a service, take it in the constructor.
- **There is no ambient context.** `AmbientExecutionContext` was removed in v2. The context
  is a parameter on every handler and interceptor, and the only way to reach it. See
  [Execution context](/ergosfare.docs/core-concepts/execution-context).

Next: [Compile-time discovery](/ergosfare.docs/core-concepts/compile-time-discovery).

guides.title: Installation
guides.description: Which Ergosfare packages you need, and why the source generator is a separate one.
guides.body:
Ergosfare v2 is the stable line on nuget.org, so a plain `dotnet add package` gets it. If you
want the in-development line instead, the [preview docs](/ergosfare.docs/preview/getting-started/installation)
cover it.

## The short version

For an application:

```bash
dotnet add package Stella.Ergosfare
dotnet add package Stella.Ergosfare.SourceGenerator
```

`Stella.Ergosfare` is a convenience bundle that pulls in the Commands, Queries and Events
modules with their DI extensions. `Stella.Ergosfare.SourceGenerator` is what produces
`RegisterGenerated()`.

{% aside type="caution" %}
The source generator is a **separate package on purpose**, but it is not optional in
practice. It is what compiles the frozen composition table and emits `RegisterGenerated()`;
without it a container has nothing to select from and every dispatch fails with
`NoHandlerFoundException`. Runtime assembly scanning was removed in v2.3 — see
[Migrating from v2.2 to v2.3](/ergosfare.docs/migration/v2.2-to-v2.3).
{% /aside %}

## Requirements

- **.NET 9.0, .NET 10.0 or .NET 11.0.** The libraries multi-target
  `net9.0;net10.0;net11.0`. The `net11.0` assets carry no extra API — they exist as proof the
  sources compile under the C# 15 compiler and hold the contract suite on .NET 11. A
  `net11.0` project without them already binds `lib/net10.0/` through roll-forward.
- **C# `latest`.** The generated registration code is deliberately conservative, but the
  abstractions use current language features.

{% aside type="note" %}
.NET 11 reaches GA on 2026-11-10. Until then the `net11.0` assets are compiled against
**preview reference packs** and will be re-packed against the GA pack once it ships. Targeting
`net9.0` or `net10.0` avoids the question entirely and loses nothing.
{% /aside %}

## Picking packages deliberately

The umbrella package is convenient, not required. Each module is independent:

| Package | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `Stella.Ergosfare` | Umbrella — Commands + Queries + Events + DI extensions |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.SourceGenerator` | Compile-time discovery, `RegisterGenerated()`, dispatch roots |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.Core.Abstractions` | `ErgosfareContext`, attributes, handler contracts |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.Commands.Abstractions` | `ICommand`, `ICommandHandler`, command interceptors |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.Queries.Abstractions` | `IQuery`, `IStreamQuery`, query handlers and interceptors |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.Events.Abstractions` | `IEvent`, `IEventHandler`, event interceptors |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.Core` | Runtime: composition catalog, pipeline plans, dispatch |
| `Stella.Ergosfare.*.Extensions.MicrosoftDependencyInjection` | `AddErgosfare`, `AddCommandModule`, module builders |

### Library that only declares messages and handlers

Reference just the abstractions. This keeps the library free of the runtime and of any DI
container dependency:

```bash
dotnet add package Stella.Ergosfare.Commands.Abstractions
```

The library needs **no registration code**. When an application that references it runs the
source generator, the generator walks referenced assemblies and registers those handlers
through the application's own `RegisterGenerated()`. See
[Compile-time discovery](/ergosfare.docs/core-concepts/compile-time-discovery).

### Application that only uses commands

```bash
dotnet add package Stella.Ergosfare.Commands
dotnet add package Stella.Ergosfare.Commands.Extensions.MicrosoftDependencyInjection
dotnet add package Stella.Ergosfare.SourceGenerator
```

## Verifying the generator is running

The generator writes a single file into your compilation. After a build you can find it at:

```
obj/gen/Stella.Ergosfare.SourceGenerator/…/ErgosfareRegistrations.g.cs
```

Open it and you should see an `internal static class ErgosfareGeneratedRegistrations` in
namespace `Stella.Ergosfare.Generated`. If `RegisterGenerated()` does not resolve in your
startup code, the usual cause is a missing using:

```csharp
using Stella.Ergosfare.Generated;
```

## Reference scanning

By default the generator also inspects referenced assemblies so that handlers shipped by
libraries register automatically. To turn that off for a project:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <ErgosfareSourceGeneratorScanReferences>false</ErgosfareSourceGeneratorScanReferences>
</PropertyGroup>
```

Next: [Quick start](/ergosfare.docs/getting-started/quick-start) wires up a command, a query
and an event in one file.

guides.title: Introduction
guides.description: Ergosfare is a source-generated, high-performance mediator for CQRS-style messaging in .NET — commands, queries and events over one pipeline model.
guides.body:
Ergosfare is a mediator for CQRS-style messaging in .NET: commands, queries and events over
one pipeline model. It is built around a single design premise — **all dispatch-shape work
happens at compile time or once per message type, never per dispatch**.

A Roslyn source generator compiles a **frozen composition table** — one immutable
composition per message type, holding its handler rows and its four interceptor stages in
execution order — and emits the registration that selects from it. Pipeline plans are
computed once per `(message type, group set)` and cached process-wide. Dispatch generics are
closed at compile time, and execution contexts are pooled. A dispatch resolves handler
*instances* from the calling DI scope and walks a pre-built plan — no reflection, no
`MakeGenericType`, no assembly scan, no `AsyncLocal`, and no per-dispatch context allocation
on the hot path.

{% aside %}
You are reading the docs for the **stable v2 line**, built from the
[`main` branch](https://github.com/stellayazilim/Ergosfare/tree/main). Work in progress lands
on the [preview line](/ergosfare.docs/preview/getting-started/introduction) first. Upgrading
from v2.2? v2.3 removed the runtime registry — see
[Migrating from v2.2 to v2.3](/ergosfare.docs/migration/v2.2-to-v2.3). Coming from v1? See
[Migrating from v1](/ergosfare.docs/migration/v1-to-v2).
{% /aside %}

## What it looks like

```csharp
using Stella.Ergosfare.Commands.Abstractions;
using Stella.Ergosfare.Core.Abstractions;

public sealed record CreateProduct(string Name) : ICommand<Guid>;

public sealed class CreateProductHandler : ICommandHandler<CreateProduct, Guid>
{
    public ValueTask<Guid> HandleAsync(CreateProduct command, ErgosfareContext context)
        => ValueTask.FromResult(Guid.NewGuid());
}
```

Nothing registers this handler by hand. The source generator finds it at compile time and
emits the registration call you wire up once at startup:

```csharp
using Stella.Ergosfare.Generated;

builder.Services.AddErgosfare(o => o
    .AddCommandModule(c => c.RegisterGenerated())
    .AddQueryModule(q => q.RegisterGenerated())
    .AddEventModule(e => e.RegisterGenerated()));
```

## Why Ergosfare

**Compile-time registration.** The generator discovers handlers in your compilation *and in
referenced assemblies*, compiles their relationships into the frozen composition table, and
emits `RegisterGenerated()`. A library's handlers register through the consuming app's
generated code with no registration code in the library at all.

**Registration is selection, not discovery.** `RegisterGenerated()` and `Register<T>()` pick
which rows of the compiled table one container runs. Repeated and overlapping selections are
harmless unions, and nothing can append a message shape after compilation — so there is no
registration window whose timing changes a running application.

**Reflection-free dispatch.** Generated dispatch roots close executor generics at compile
time, and pipeline plans pre-close generic handler types. `MakeGenericType` survives only as
a fallback for message types the generator could not root, chiefly open generics.

**Allocation you can account for.** Pooled execution contexts, a `ValueTask`-first surface
and generated plans put a no-result command at 19.9 ns / 24 B and a result query at
24.0 ns / 24 B per dispatch. See [Performance](/ergosfare.docs/advanced/performance) for the
measured shapes and how to read them.

**Nested dispatch, safely.** `context.CreateScope()` gives a handler an isolated child
context with inherited cancellation for mediator calls inside handlers — the pattern
ambient-state mediators cannot offer safely.

**No ambient state.** The execution context is a parameter, never an `AsyncLocal`. Nothing
about a dispatch is discoverable from thread-local storage, which is what makes nested and
parallel dispatch predictable.

**Native AOT and trimming.** Every construct is referenced statically via `typeof`, and
dispatch roots anchor every generic instantiation — including `record struct` messages,
which shared generic code cannot cover.

**Modular.** Commands, Queries and Events are independent packages over a shared core.
A library that only declares messages needs just the relevant `.Abstractions` package.

## How a dispatch fits together

```
compile time                    once per (message type, groups)         every dispatch
────────────                    ───────────────────────────────         ──────────────
source generator         ──►    composition ─► selection ─► plan     ──►  pooled context rented
  frozen composition table        │                                          │
  dispatch roots emitted          │  six fixed stages, pre-ordered           │  executor closed over runtime type
  RegisterGenerated()             │  (direct-first, weight-ordered)          │  handler resolved from calling scope
                                  └─ closed generic types pre-computed       └─ pre → main → post/exception → final
```

- **Composition and selection.** The generator compiles one `FrozenComposition` per message
  type into a process-wide table. Registration selects which of its participant rows this
  container runs — `RegisterGenerated()` in bulk, `Register<T>()` one at a time. Selection is
  a union, so the two are safe to combine and repeat.
- **Pipeline plan.** Six fixed stages per message: main handlers (split direct/indirect) and
  four interceptor stages, each a pre-ordered array. Direct entries come first, then
  covariant matches ordered by weight. Group filters and `[ExcludeFromPipeline]` are applied
  here, once.
- **Dispatch.** The mediator rents a pooled context, looks up the cached executor for the
  message's runtime type, and walks the plan. Handler resolution belongs to the dispatcher —
  the execution context deliberately exposes **no** service provider.

## Where to go next

- [Installation](/ergosfare.docs/getting-started/installation) — which packages you actually need.
- [Quick start](/ergosfare.docs/getting-started/quick-start) — a command, a query and an event, end to end.
- [Compile-time discovery](/ergosfare.docs/core-concepts/compile-time-discovery) — where `RegisterGenerated()` comes from.
- [Migrating from v2.2 to v2.3](/ergosfare.docs/migration/v2.2-to-v2.3) — what v2.3 removed, and the replacement for each.
- [Migrating from v1](/ergosfare.docs/migration/v1-to-v2) — if you are still on the v1 line.

{% aside type="note" %}
Stuck on something? Open an issue on
[GitHub](https://github.com/stellayazilim/ergosfare/issues).
{% /aside %}
